newsitem.title: LEBANON: Germany to take back plastic waste.
newsitem.headline: Germany to take back plastic waste.

text.p: A German government-related agency will take back 680 tonnes of plastic waste illegally shipped to Beirut in 1996, German embassy Counselor Wolfgang Lerke said on Wednesday.

"The Solidarity Fund For Re-Exporting Waste, a German private agency supervised by the government of Bonn, decided last Friday to ship to Germany the 36 containers for final incineration there," Lerke told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Implementation will be delayed for some time to arrange technical aspects related to the burning of the shipment, he said.

"The decision has been taken. Our ambassador announced it to Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri yesterday. It will take some time to implement the decision because a proper site where the waste can be incinerated must be found," he added.
He said the operation would be financed by the Solidarity Fund.
"We are very happy to take them back. This is very important for Lebanon and equally important is that they will be immediately burned in Germany," Lerke said.

Last month, a Lebanese investigative magistrate demanded five to 10 years imprisonment for three Lebanese on charges of illegally importing the 36 containers of "polluted plastic waste and toxic chemicals that endanger public health".
The shipment has been held at the port since August.
The international environmental organisation Greenpeace has said the shipment includes a mixture of plastic wastes contaminated with laboratory chemicals, pesticides and chemical fertilisers.
